text:
nina: Quick thread: finalizing 'SurgeGuard' packaging for startup customers. Topic: tiering, limits, pilot incentives, and negotiation boundaries. Customers ask for 4x throughput, unlimited bursts during launches. Need concrete pilot terms and a fallback plan.

ash: Tech reality: 4x sustained is risky. Recommend offering 2 tiers: SurgeGuard-Basic (2x sustain + small burst pool) and SurgeGuard-Enterprise (3x sustain, larger burst credits, dedicated queues). No unlimited bursts. Example knobs:
```
tenant_hard_qps=3000
tenant_soft_qps=6000
burst_window_sec=900
burst_credits_month=200000
```
We need cluster policing for simultaneous bursts.

ash: Telemetry: surgeguard.qps, surgeguard.burst_used, surgeguard.throttle_events.

tom: Sales: For pilots, offer 50% off month 1 and include 50k burst credits. Pricing suggestion:
SurgeGuard-Basic: $1500/mo + $0.09 per 1k tokens overage
SurgeGuard-Enterprise: $6000/mo + $0.04 per 1k tokens overage, 200k credits included
Negotiation levers: burst credits, commit term, support response time. Non-negotiable: unlimited burst.

sales-ops: Billing needs a new SKU: surgeguard.basic and surgeguard.enterprise. Meter: burst_credits_used, tier. Also tag pilot discounts to invoice metadata.

legal-bot: Reminder: any custom support/SLA promises must be escalated. Suggested clause: "Burst credits are allocated monthly and do not guarantee absolute availability; provider reserves the right to throttle to protect platform stability."

nina: Launch checklist for pilot: console UI for burst balance, billing line-item, telemetry + alerting, runbook for cross-tenant exhaustion, two signed pilots. Target pilot in 5 weeks.

ops-bot: Feature flag "surgeguard" enabled in staging for testing.

ash: Note: consider making burst credits measurable in compute-units rather than tokens to simplify multi-model customers.

nina: Good point. We'll prototype CU conversion in the billing test. Any objections to the pricing bands above?

tom: None from sales. We'll start outreach to Alpha customers.

nina: I'll drop the PRD and pricing one-pager tomorrow. Thanks!
